text:
Alex DeBrincat dropped the gloves with Florida's Sam Bennett last week, and the reaction in Detroit said a lot about where the Red Wings are: fans calling for him to be the next captain, and Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom writing about what it means to be a leader. With Dylan Larkin refusing to play until he's traded, the team has been looking for someone to carry it.

On the scoresheet, DeBrincat is in a quiet patch: no points in six games and one goal in his last ten, during a stretch when Detroit lost five straight. He has 16 points in 21 games after 41 goals last season. His chances have thinned a bit in that stretch, but for the season the process is strong: Detroit takes 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, almost 10 points better than without him.

He was Evolving-Hockey's 6th-best forward by wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile for chances from the slot. Our talent range projects about 35 goals. He's still the scorer; Detroit needs him to be more than that this year.
